claim: The Production front 'How (in question)' fits どうやって, which I learned in Lesson 7 as plain 'How', just as well as どう, and nothing on the front points to impressions.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Grammar & Function Words / How (in question)'. Answer: どう. Ledger: chapter-7-extras 'どうやって | How' (used in どうやってしごとにいきますか, 'How do you go to work?'), and chapter-7 'なんでいきますか | How will you go?'.
fix: Add a hint that separates the two, e.g. 'asking for an opinion or impression, as in How was it?', or gloss it 'How (what was it like)'.
verdictReason: Ledger: chapter-7-extras ships どうやって with the bare gloss 'How' and no hint; 'How (in question)' does not separate it, since どうやって is also only ever used in a question. The authoring rules make a cue mandatory on an English-gloss collision. 'in question' is the book's gloss, so the fix is a hint, not a regloss.

claim: The Production hint prints the answer in kana and romaji on the front that asks for it.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Time / (Number of) hours / after a number, as in 2じかん (ni-jikan)'. Answer: じかん.
fix: Keep the hint on the Recognition face only, or reword the Production hint without the Japanese, e.g. 'the suffix you put after a number, as in two hours'.
verdictReason: Rendered: the `scene` 'after a number, as in 2じかん (ni-jikan)' prints on the Production FRONT above an answer of じかん, in kana and romaji. The rules say a scene must never contain the answer. Preflight flagged this scene only for romaji style, not as a leak.

claim: The note calls あるきます the 'Dictionary/plain form of the verb'. It is the polite ます form; the dictionary form is あるく. The learner has only ever seen ます forms, so the label matches nothing taught, and the Reader confirms it is false.
evidence: Card note: 'Dictionary/plain form of the verb; different from あるいて (aruite, "on foot") from Lesson 7, the adverbial form...'. Book VOCABULARY: 'あるきます walk' (every verb listed in ます form). Ledger: いきます / いきません / いきました taught as the ordinary polite forms; chapter-15 later uses 'dictionary form (plain, casual)' in its technical sense.
fix: Drop 'Dictionary/plain form of the verb;' and keep the contrast between the verb あるきます (walk) and Lesson 7's あるいて (on foot).
verdictReason: Checked the rendered note and the book's vocabulary list: あるきます is the ます form, not the dictionary form (あるく). Both roles found the same sentence; merged under the Reader's kind because the label is false, not merely unverifiable. Should-fix: chapter-15 later teaches 'dictionary form (plain, casual)' as a distinct thing, so this label will collide with it.

claim: The note calls きれいでした its 'plain past form'. It is the polite (です-style) past; the plain past would be きれいだった. The learner has never been shown a 'plain' form and knows でした only as Lesson 2's polite 'Was'.
evidence: Card note: 'きれい (kirei) is a な-adjective; きれいでした is its plain past form.' Book GRAMMAR 1 table headed 'As predicate: adjective +です', past aff. きれいでした. Ledger chapter-2: 'でした | Was'.
fix: Change 'plain past form' to 'past form' (or 'polite past form').
verdictReason: Checked note and book table: きれいでした sits under 'adjective + です', the polite set. This deck uses 'plain' in its technical sense elsewhere (chapter-10-extras 'plain negative じゃない', chapter-15 hint 'dictionary form (plain, casual)'), so the label is wrong by the deck's own usage, not just loose. Merged; Reader's should-fix kept since the mislabel will contradict later cards.

claim: The note calls たいへんでした its 'plain past form'. It is the polite (です-style) past, using the same でした as every other past the learner has met.
evidence: Card note: 'な-adjective meaning hard or tough...; たいへんでした (taihen deshita) is its plain past form.' Book EXERCISES I-B table: たいへんです / たいへんじゃありません / たいへんでした / たいへんじゃありませんでした, all in the adjective + です predicate set.
verdictReason: Same mislabel as kirei-deshita, checked against the rendered note and the EXERCISES I-B table (polite です set). Merged; should-fix for the same reason.

claim: The note calls たのしかったです its 'plain past form'. With です it is the polite past; the plain past is たのしかった. The learner has only met です-ending sentences and cannot tell what 'plain' means.
evidence: Card note: 'い-adjective; たのしかったです (tanoshikatta desu) is its plain past form.' Book EXERCISES I-A table: たのしいです / たのしくないです / たのしかったです / たのしくなかったです under 'As predicate: adjective +です'.
verdictReason: Same mislabel, checked against the rendered note and the EXERCISES I-A table. Merged; should-fix for the same reason.

claim: The English says 'really good', and the deck taught me ほんとうに as 'Really' and とても as 'Very', so I answer ほんとうによかったです and the card marks me wrong.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'It was really good. / answering how the concert was'. Answer: とてもよかったです. Ledger chapter-10: 'とても | Very', 'ほんとうに | Really' (the とても note says とても leans toward 'very').
fix: Gloss it 'It was very good.' to match とても.
verdictReason: Card is aiSuggested with no book English for this exercise item; the book's own rendering of the same sentence in SPEAKING PRACTICE 2 is 'It was very nice.' Ledger chapter-10 glosses とても 'Very' and ほんとうに 'Really', and the とても note itself says とても leans toward 'very', so 'really good' points the learner at ほんとうによかったです. Polish stands.

claim: The bare English 'Date' could mean a calendar date, which the deck has already taught me through にち and なんにち. Nothing on the front says it means a romantic outing.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Other / Date'. Answer: デート. Ledger chapter-7: 'なんにち | What day', 'りょこうはなんにちからなんにちまでですか | What dates does the trip run from and to?'.
fix: Gloss it 'Date (going out with someone)' or add that as a hint.
verdictReason: No competing target: grep of every cards.json in the collection finds no other card glossed 'Date' and no calendar-date noun taught (にち is 'Day (suffix)', なんにち 'What day'), so デート is the only word the learner has for 'date' in any sense. The gloss is the book's own ('デート date'), and the same unit's 'Yesterday's date wasn't fun.' cards fix the sense.

claim: 'Really delicious' sends me to ほんとうに ('Really'), but the answer uses とても ('Very').
evidence: Production FRONT: 'It was really delicious. / answering how the tempura you ate in Asakusa was'. Answer: とてもおいしかったです. Ledger chapter-10-extras: 'はい、とてもおいしいです | Yes, it's very delicious.'
verdictReason: The collision is real (ledger: とても 'Very', ほんとうに 'Really'), but this English is the book's own translation of the same line in SPEAKING PRACTICE 3 ('とても おいしかったです' = 'It was really delicious.'), so the card is faithful. Settled by an owner call on whether a sentence gloss may depart from the book's translation to keep the deck's とても/ほんとうに distinction consistent; if yes, regloss 'very' as the fix says.

claim: 'Really beautiful' asks for ほんとうに, and this same unit's ex11-hontou-ni-kirei-desu-ne uses 'really' for ほんとうに, but the answer is とても.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'It was really beautiful. / answering how climbing Mt. Fuji was'. Answer: とてもきれいでした. Same unit: 'ほんとうにきれいですね | It really is beautiful, isn't it?'.
verdictReason: Same as ex11-totemo-oishikatta-desu: the collision is real, but 'It was really beautiful.' is the book's own translation of Emma's TARGET DIALOGUE line 'とても きれいでした', so the card is faithful to the book. Same owner call settles it.

claim: The English starts with 'Really?', which is exactly the gloss the deck gave ほんとうですか, while the answer uses そうですか, which I learned as 'I see. / Is that so?'.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Really? I'm glad to hear that. / replying to a colleague who has just told you the souvenir you gave her was delicious'. Answer: そうですか、よかったです. Ledger chapter-9: 'ほんとうですか | Really?'; chapter-3: 'そうですか | I see. / Is that so?'.
fix: Gloss it 'Oh, is that so? I'm glad to hear that.' (or 'I see. I'm glad.') so it points to そうですか.
verdictReason: Ledger: chapter-9 ships ほんとうですか with the bare gloss 'Really?'; chapter-3 ships そうですか as 'I see. / Is that so?'. The book's own English for this SPEAKING PRACTICE 3 line is 'Good. I'm glad to hear that.', so 'Really?' is the deck's choice, not the book's, and it is the exact gloss of a different card. Should-fix stands.

claim: With no scene, 'This is a souvenir from Hakone.' makes me say これははこねのおみやげです, and the card's own note says that's the version for a different situation. Nothing on the front tells me I'm handing the gift over.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Travel & Tourism / This is a souvenir from Hakone.' Answer: これ、はこねのおみやげです. Note: 'これははこねのおみやげです (kore wa hakone no omiyage desu) would be the version used when they are already looking at it.'
fix: Add a scene such as 'handing a gift to a colleague as you give it', so the comma form is the one the front asks for.
verdictReason: Rendered Production FRONT is 'Travel & Tourism / This is a souvenir from Hakone.' with no scene or hint. Everything the ledger taught (これは…です since Lesson 2) produces これははこねのおみやげです, which the card's own note and the book's NOTES 3 describe as the other situation. Book context (SPEAKING PRACTICE 2) is handing the gift over with どうぞ, so a scene is available that does not paraphrase the answer.

claim: The note says all of いい's negative and past forms are built from よく, but the past affirmative よかったです is not (it is よ + かった), and the sibling card yokatta-desu-good says the stem is よ.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 1 table: いいです, よくないです*, よかったです*, よくなかったです* (* exceptional inflection). Card note: "its negative and past forms are built from よく, not いく." Card yokatta-desu-good note: "the past of いい (ii, good) uses the stem よ (yo)".
fix: Say the other forms are built on よ (よくない, よかった, よくなかった) rather than on い.
verdictReason: Note says いい's 'negative and past forms are built from よく'. よくないです and よくなかったです are; よかったです is よ + かった, and the sibling card yokatta-desu-good's note says the stem is よ. Book GRAMMAR 1 marks all three as exceptional without naming よく. Polish stands.

claim: NOTES 1 says the くらい in どのくらい may also be pronounced ぐらい, and no card tells the learner that どのぐらい is the same question.
evidence: Book, NOTES 1: "Here, どのくらい means 'how long.' くらい may also be pronounced ぐらい." Card dono-kurai note covers only the answer: "commonly answered with a ぐらい (gurai) phrase". The gurai card notes the reverse variant (ぐらい may be くらい) but not どのぐらい.
fix: Add to the dono-kurai note that it may also be said どのぐらい (dono gurai).
verdictReason: Book NOTES 1: 'Here, どのくらい means "how long." くらい may also be pronounced ぐらい.' grep of every cards.json in the collection: どのぐらい appears nowhere. The gurai card's note gives only the reverse variant (ぐらい may be くらい). Polish stands.

claim: The hint, shown on the Production front, calls どういたしまして a little stiff and says people usually brush thanks aside; the book presents it as the ordinary reply, said by the host in the lesson's own dialogue, with no such caveat.
evidence: Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE 1: Emma: "きょうは どうも ありがとうございました。" Sasaki: "どういたしまして。" VOCABULARY: "どういたしまして。 You're welcome." Card hint: "a little stiff; in everyday talk people usually just brush the thanks aside".
fix: Remove the hint, or replace it with the book's context (a host replying to a guest's thanks).
verdictReason: Rendered: the hint 'a little stiff; in everyday talk people usually just brush the thanks aside' shows on the Production FRONT and the Recognition back. The book gives どういたしまして plainly as Sasaki's reply in SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 and glosses it 'You're welcome.' with no caveat. No other card in the collection is glossed 'You're welcome' (chapter-4's いらっしゃいませ is 'May I help you?, Welcome.'), so the hint is not resolving a collision, which is the only job the rules give a hint. Polish stands.

claim: Most of the note (the topic reading of きのうは and a claim that きのうのおみやげ would sound as if picking one gift out from others) is not in the book, which only explains the past-tense thanks.
evidence: Book, NOTES 2: "When expressing thanks for something that has ended, the past tense of ありがとうございます is used." Card note: "...きのうのおみやげ (kinō no omiyage, 'yesterday's souvenir') is grammatical, but it labels the gift by its day, as if picking it out from other souvenirs."
fix: Cut the note to the book's point: past-tense ありがとうございました thanks someone for something already done; drop the きのうのおみやげ comparison.
verdictReason: Book NOTES 2 supports only the past-tense-thanks point. The きのうは-as-topic reading is the author's own (defensible from KS1's きのうは, but not stated), and the closing claim that きのうのおみやげ 'labels the gift by its day, as if picking it out from other souvenirs' is a judgement the book nowhere makes and the learner cannot check. Polish; trimming the last sentence loses nothing the book teaches.
